title: -Os miscompile of hcs08_vformat: %u consumes 4 bytes instead of 2
status: FIXED - root cause found, two defects, both fixed and verified on silicon
severity: high - silently wrong output from correct C; no diagnostic
found_by: running the HCS08 SDK's printf on real silicon (MC9S08AW60)

root_cause.summary: A conditional branch was reading flags written by an instruction other than its compare, so `if (longs == 0)` always took its non-zero side and every %u ran the 32-bit converter.
the_block: lda  $25,x    ; base - lda sets N and Z, so this overwrites the test
root_cause.why_it_always_failed: base is 8, 10 or 16 for o/u/x/X - never zero - so the bne was always taken and the wide path always ran.
chain: MachineCSE's PRE hoisted a ZEXT8to16 of `base` into the block dominating both conversion paths, and placed it before the terminator - which is after the compare.
HCS08FuseCompareBranch only ever looked at std::prev(branch), so it found the extend rather than the compare, declined to fuse, and left the pair split.
Register allocation then filled the same gap, exactly as that pass's own header comment predicts: a reload (lda, sets N and Z) for `base` and a spill (sthx, sets N and Z) of the extended value.
The branch read those flags instead of the compare's.

defects_fixed.what: HCS08FuseCompareBranch gave up whenever anything sat between a compare and its branch.
defects_fixed.fix: Walk back to whatever last wrote NZV. If that is a foldable flag setter and everything in the gap neither reads nor writes either flag group, nor defines a register the compare reads, nor conflicts over memory, sink the compare down to the branch and fuse. Otherwise leave it alone, as before.

defects_fixed.what: clrh was modelled as writing no flags. It writes them like the rest of the clr family: V and N cleared, Z set.
defects_fixed.consequence: ZEXT8to16 is `tax; clrh`, so every byte-to-word zero extension silently clobbered NZV. That is what let MachineCSE put one between a compare and its branch in the first place, and it would equally have corrupted a SELECT8/SELECT16, which read NZV and which fusion does not protect.
defects_fixed.fix: ZEXT8to16 declares Defs = [NZV]; CLRHd declares Defs = [H, NZV]; the expandPostRAPseudo BuildMI for CLRH adds the implicit NZV def.
defects_fixed.measured_not_quoted: On an MC9S08AW60, with Z left 0 by an unequal compare, tpa reads back $6A after clrh and $68 after tax - identical but for bit 1, which is Z. See test/target/t_clrh_flags.c in the SDK, where tax is the control.

how_it_was_found.the_decisive_observation: The recorded symptom `u=1720980` is larger than 65535. utoa16_rev takes a 16-bit unsigned and divides with __udivhi3, so it cannot emit that value at all - only utoa_wide_rev can. So the wide converter was *running*, which meant the branch was mis-taken rather than a narrow conversion over-reading.
how_it_was_found.what_had_blocked_it: The earlier conclusion that 'no narrow conversion site was rewritten into a wide one' was sound as far as it went - the counts of __udivhi3 and __udivsi3 call sites were right - but it was read as exonerating the branch, which it did not. Both conversion loops were present and correct; the selection between them was not.
how_it_was_found.the_mechanical_step: -print-after-all at -Os, then for each machine pass, for each conditional branch, walk back to the nearest NZV def and report it when it is not a compare. That named MachineCSE on the first try.

verification: llvm/test/CodeGen/HCS08/cmp-branch-fusion-gap.mir - four cases: a gap that closes (aix, which genuinely leaves the CCR alone), and three that must not fuse (an extend, an arithmetic flag write, and a redefinition of what the compare reads). Confirmed to fail without the pass fix.
Whole-file scan of hcs08_vformat's -Os assembly for any NZV writer between a compare and its branch: 1 before the fix, 0 after.
SDK `make check` - 370 host checks, 3 ucsim target tests, the self-call check.
Silicon, MC9S08AW60, with HCS08_PRINTF_LONG=1 - the configuration that failed: 5/5, t_pf2.c included. RAM is poisoned with 0xEE before each run, so a stale answer cannot pass.
libhcs08_aw60.a is 6034 bytes before and after; the flag modelling change costs nothing here.

follow_up.sdk_default: HCS08_PRINTF_LONG=0 was shipped as the SDK default only to dodge this bug. It can be reconsidered now, which is an SDK decision rather than a backend one.
follow_up.residual_risk: Spill and reload code still does not consult NZV liveness - LLVM assumes throughout that it cannot clobber flags, and on this machine every reload is an lda. Fusion is what makes that safe, so it has to reach every conditional branch. The .mir test is what keeps it honest.
follow_up.ucsim: Still cannot run t_pf2.c: it does not implement ldhx/sthx n,sp (0x9E FE/FF), which is the 16-bit stack-argument path varargs use. The test stays SILICON_ONLY.

llvm.note: build with ninja inside `toolbox run -c fedora`; make/ninja/cmake are not on the host

silicon.part: MC9S08AW60 on a Valco/VICI UA display board
silicon.bus_clock_note: MEASURED: with --reset-into-bdm the BDC reports CLKSW set and 4.000 MHz, which is the bus. Do not use 3888000 - that is the STOCK firmware's clock, which configures the ICG; SDK crt0 does not.
silicon.programmer: Glasgow revC3, applet debug-hcs08 at /var/home/atomicdog/repo/glasgow (branch wip-applet.debug.hcs08)
silicon.wiring: BKGD=A0, RESET=A1, ground to BDM pin 2, port A at 3.3 V. Serial (if needed): board TX -> A3, board RX -> A2, uart applet with --rx A3 --tx A2 -b 9600.
quirks: After `program` the PC sits in the applet's FLASH routine in the high-page register block (~$180E), NOT at the reset vector. You must --reset-into-bdm before `run` or you execute the register file as code.
RAM survives a reset, which is what lets silicon.py poison it before running.

gotchas_kept_because_they_cost_time.trap: The SDK's 370 host printf tests pass throughout, before and after
gotchas_kept_because_they_cost_time.detail: They use the host libc as an oracle. The host's int is 32-bit, so a converter reading 32 where it should read 16 is simply correct there. The host oracle is structurally blind to target argument layout.

gotchas_kept_because_they_cost_time.trap: -O0 cannot be used as a control
gotchas_kept_because_they_cost_time.detail: hcs08_vformat's frame reaches SP+277 against the 256-byte ceiling and the backend refuses. That refusal is correct and unrelated. A build script that does not check for a failed compile will silently test a stale .o and report a false PASS - this happened once.
A grep filter listing bne/beq/jmp but not bcc made a correct narrow loop look like it had no exit test. Dump whole blocks before concluding.
It gates the wide converter AND changes FMT_DIGITS 12->8, hence the frame. Any experiment toggling it is confounded unless FMT_DIGITS is pinned.

llvm.what: [HCS08] Add a disable flag for the compare/branch fusion pass (added while chasing this; the differing failure it produced - `width` also corrupt - was the clue that several locals were wrong, i.e. a flags problem rather than one bad branch)
[HCS08] Say there are no jump tables, so none is built (unrelated bug found by the same printf)
[HCS08] Let inline assembly ask for a register (which is what t_clrh_flags.c needs to read the CCR with tpa)
